Demand from population groups and group-specific rates

Source: R/08-calc_demand.R
calc_demand.Rd

Multiplies population counts in each group (for example, age bands) by a group-specific rate, sums over groups and applies a common scale (for example, the share of cases that use a given service): $$D_i = s \sum_b r_b \, P_{ib}.$$

Usage

calc_demand(
  groups,
  rates,
  scale = 1,
  total = NULL,
  fallback = c("mean", "error")
)

Arguments

groups

A multilayer SpatRaster with one named layer per group, or a numeric matrix with one named column per group and one row per origin. A missing group value counts as zero; a cell whose groups are all missing has missing demand (unless total supplies it).

rates

A named numeric vector of nonnegative rates, one per group. Every group must have a rate (use 0 for groups without demand) and every rate a group.

scale

A positive multiplier applied to every cell (default 1).

total

Optional total population: a one-layer SpatRaster on the same grid as groups, or a numeric vector with one value per row of groups.

fallback

What to do with cells that have a total but no group population: "mean" uses the overall rate, "error" stops.

Value

Demand with the same layout as a single group: a one-layer SpatRaster or a numeric vector. Attributes record the overall implied rate (implied_rate, before scale), the number of fallback cells (fallback_cells) and the rates used.

Details

Gridded products often provide group counts and a total population that do not sum exactly. With total, each cell's group composition is applied to its total instead: \(D_i = s \, T_i \sum_b r_b P_{ib} / \sum_b P_{ib}\). Cells with a total but no group population use the overall rate across all cells (fallback = "mean") or stop (fallback = "error").

See also

Other experimental allocation workflow: bootstrap_allocation(), calc_travel_time(), check_allocation(), clm_allocation(), compare_allocations(), decay_kernel(), evaluate_allocation(), fit_allocation(), huff_allocation(), predict_allocation(), prepare_allocation()

Examples

library(terra)

# Two age groups on the Cornwall population grid: under 15 and 15 or over
pop <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif")
groups <- c(pop * 0.16, pop * 0.84)
names(groups) <- c("age_0_14", "age_15_plus")

# A condition affecting 0.5% of people aged 15 or over, 80% of whom use
# the service, applied to the total population grid
demand <- calc_demand(groups, c(age_0_14 = 0, age_15_plus = 0.005),
                      scale = 0.8, total = pop)
attr(demand, "implied_rate")
#> [1] 0.0042
